items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: when Burgess decided to leave, we felt that Jim would be worth a try on lead... He made two entrances into our band. The first time he came as a second trombonist to Bobby Burgess

ctx.x: And yet, when Burgess decided to leave, we felt that Jim would be worth a try on lead. And this evidently was the move that he needed and it turned out to be utterly fantastic. His rise was that of a meteor, in other words, it seemed like overnight he just started to grow and leaps and bounds as far as his abilities on the trombone.
You thought he was a find of the last 25 years.
